question: How should an LLM reasoning system modularize initial generation, conditional revision, and candidate selection so that revisions can change strategy without discarding a better original answer?

key_findings.claim: SCREWS factors test-time reasoning into Sampling, Conditional Resampling, and Selection, exposing rollback and heterogeneous revision as independent design decisions.
key_findings.evidence: The initial method produces a provisional answer; a gate decides whether to revise it and may use another reasoning method or tool; a selector compares original and revised candidates. Existing self-refinement, voting, decomposition, and tool-feedback systems can be expressed as configurations of these modules.

key_findings.claim: Changing reasoning method during revision is more reliable on GSM8K than simply repeating the original method in the reported prompts.
key_findings.evidence: CoT improves from 71.64% to 73.00% when revised by CoT and to 73.69% with generated subquestions. Generated-subquestion sampling improves from 71.87% to 73.99% when revised by CoT but drops to 71.26% when revised homogeneously; oracle-subquestion sampling similarly drops from 78.62% to 78.24% under homogeneous revision.

key_findings.claim: Candidate selection can recover from harmful revisions, but the large gap to oracle selection shows that the few-shot LLM selector remains a bottleneck.
key_findings.evidence: Selecting between independent CoT and generated-subquestion answers raises GSM8K accuracy from about 71.6-71.9% to 74.90%, while a perfect selector would reach 85.36%. Selection between original and conditional revisions adds up to about one point in subquestion settings, and conditional resampling runs on only 5-15% of examples there.

key_findings.claim: Internal revision cannot repair missing facts reliably; external evidence is the relevant new signal.
key_findings.evidence: On StrategyQA, homogeneous internal resampling lowers CoT from 77.18% to 74.54% and generated subquestions from 78.16% to 74.69%. Supplying dataset-provided facts during conditional revision raises them to 79.02% and 80.40%, although facts are a simulated perfect retrieval result rather than an end-to-end retriever evaluation.

key_findings.claim: The code-debugging gain is striking but too small-sample to establish broad robustness, and extra revision iterations show rapidly diminishing returns.
key_findings.evidence: Answer-only rises from 73.52% to 88.23% after resampling and selection on just 33 held-out AutoDebugging examples. On GSM8K, a first oracle-subquestion revision/selection reaches 79.22%, while second and third iterations reach only 79.45% and 79.52% at added cost.

method.core_idea: Preserve multiple reasoning candidates and make revision policy, revision mechanism, and final choice swappable rather than assuming each new answer is an improvement.
method.mechanism: Prompted ChatGPT or GPT-4 generates an answer using direct, chain-of-thought, or subquestion reasoning. A binary decision prompt selectively invokes same-method, different-method, or fact-conditioned revision. A few-shot LLM selector, fixed rule, majority vote, or oracle then chooses among candidates.
assumptions: Prompted LLM judgments can detect when revision is needed and which candidate is better.
Exact-match task labels reflect reasoning quality sufficiently for configuration comparison.
Dataset-provided StrategyQA facts approximate a deployable retrieval tool.
The marginal token-count cost is an adequate proxy for latency and monetary cost.

techniques.role: Avoids paying for revision on every example and limits gratuitous answer changes.
Switches between chain of thought and decomposition so a second attempt does not repeat the same failure mode.
Retains the original answer and permits rejecting a harmful revision.
Injects missing evidence only when an initial answer is flagged for revision.

evaluations.metric: exact-match accuracy and average prompt/output tokens
evaluations.result: Heterogeneous revision generally beats homogeneous revision; selector gains are real but far below oracle upper bounds, and targeted revision can improve the cost-accuracy frontier.
evaluations.baseline: CoT, generated/oracle subquestions, homogeneous resampling, independent sampling, voting, and oracle selection.

evaluations.setting: First 490 StrategyQA training examples as evaluation data
evaluations.result: Internal revision frequently degrades accuracy; dataset-provided facts during revision improve results by roughly two points over initial internal sampling in key settings.
evaluations.baseline: Internal versus fact-conditioned revision and several sampling strategies.

evaluations.result: Answer-only sampling plus revision and selection reaches 88.23% from 73.52%, but the test is too small for precise generalization claims.
evaluations.baseline: Answer-only, CoT, resampling, and selection combinations.

limitations: Results depend on dated proprietary model snapshots, hand-designed prompts, and only three tasks.
The 33-example code test has high statistical uncertainty, while StrategyQA uses part of its training split for evaluation.
Oracle subquestions and provided StrategyQA facts can leak solution-relevant supervision and do not measure real retrieval errors.
The framework does not learn a router or selector end to end; configuration search and calibration are left to future work.
Token counts omit parallelism, tool latency, API pricing differences, and selector failure severity.
failure_modes: The revision gate misses an incorrect answer, so no corrective signal is sought.
Generator and selector share a misconception and confidently retain or introduce the same error.
A heterogeneous method changes formatting rather than the underlying reasoning failure.
Retrieved evidence is irrelevant or false, making tool-conditioned revision worse than the original.
Repeated revision creates oscillation or false correction while cost grows.
reusable_insights: Never overwrite the initial candidate before the revision has been independently evaluated.
Revision diversity should target causal failure modes, not merely sample-temperature diversity.
Route external tools to knowledge-deficit cases and measure retrieval-plus-revision end to end.
Report correct-to-wrong regressions and oracle-selector headroom, not only final accuracy.
open_questions: Can a calibrated learned router predict which reasoning method or tool has positive expected value per unit cost?
How should selectors be trained to avoid correlated errors with the generator?
Do heterogeneous revisions transfer across open models, adversarial distribution shift, and long-horizon agents?
Can outcome and process verifiers reduce oracle-selection headroom without introducing reward hacking?

competitive_landscape.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
competitive_landscape.difference: Self-Refine iterates feedback and revision from one LLM across seven tasks and reports broad gains. SCREWS makes selection and method-switching explicit, showing why blindly accepting each refinement can regress, but evaluates fewer tasks and relies on hand-selected configurations.

competitive_landscape.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Reflexion stores verbal feedback across environment trials for sequential decision making and coding. SCREWS instead decomposes a within-instance answer-revision workflow and emphasizes rollback selection and heterogeneous reasoning methods.

competitive_landscape.title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
competitive_landscape.difference: CRITIC integrates search, code execution, and APIs into iterative critique/correction across tasks. SCREWS provides a cleaner abstract slot for such tools and a rollback selector, but its StrategyQA experiment supplies oracle facts rather than evaluating tool acquisition failures.

competitive_landscape.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
competitive_landscape.difference: Huang et al. systematically show intrinsic self-correction often fails or degrades reasoning without external feedback. SCREWS independently exposes the same regression risk and proposes candidate preservation, method switching, and evidence injection rather than treating self-correction as a monolithic capability.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing LLM Reasoning via Critique Models with Test-Time and Training-Time Supervision
competitive_landscape.difference: This later work trains a separate step-level mathematical critic on tens of thousands of critiques and uses it at test and train time. It addresses SCREWS' weak few-shot selection bottleneck, but is specialized and substantially more training-intensive than a modular black-box wrapper.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference after current comparison: SCREWS' enduring contribution is the explicit separation of generation, conditional revision, and selection, plus empirical evidence that strategy switching and rollback matter. The components individually predate it, and later tool-based and trained-critic systems go further; its value is a human-readable design vocabulary and diagnostic matrix rather than a new learning algorithm.
reviewer_notes: Reviewed all 22 extracted pages, including prompts, token-cost appendix, every task table, selection upper bounds, model-snapshot details, and examples. Five direct and subsequent primary arXiv competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
